name: Riga
title: Riga Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement for Ships
description: Ultrasonic thickness measurement in Riga for bulk carriers, timber ships and feeders on the Daugava: hull structure gauging, ESP and renewal survey work.
h1: Ship Hull Gauging and Thickness Measurement in Riga
intro: The Freeport of Riga stretches along both banks of the Daugava, with berths for timber, wood pellets, grain, containers and liquid bulk. Bulk carriers and general cargo ships often spend days alongside, which leaves time for hold, tank and deck gauging between loading stages. Our team comes from India to Riga for ESP, renewal-survey and pre-purchase gauging, and the city's central position makes it a practical first stop on a round of Baltic ports.

highlights.p: Riga's terminals line the lower Daugava from the city centre to the river mouth. Ships lie alongside in low-salinity water through long cargo stays, which suits hold and double-bottom gauging between loading phases.

Wood pellets, sawn timber, wood chips and grain move through Riga's bulk and general cargo terminals. Grab and loader damage in the holds of older bulk carriers makes frame and tank-top gauging a common need.

Riga International Airport and the city's road links sit between Tallinn, Ventspils, Liepāja and Klaipėda. One mobilisation can cover several ships across the Baltic states when their port stays line up.

port.h: Freeport of Riga: berths, cargoes and port stays
p: The Freeport of Riga is a river port. Its terminals are spread along both banks of the Daugava, from the quays near the city centre down to the river mouth on the Gulf of Riga, and ships navigate the river channel to reach them. The cargo mix is broad: timber and wood products, wood pellets and chips, grain and agricultural products, containers through the city's container terminals, general and project cargo, and liquid bulk. A passenger terminal near the centre takes cruise calls in the summer season.

Trade patterns have shifted in recent years. Transit flows of coal and other bulk from the east, once a large share of Riga's throughput, fell away under EU sanctions, and the port has leaned more heavily on Latvian and regional exports, especially forest products and grain, and on container feeder services linking Riga with the North Sea hubs. The fleet that calls reflects that: handysize and smaller bulk carriers, multipurpose and general cargo ships, timber carriers with deck cargo, container feeders and product tankers. Many of these are older ships whose renewal surveys bring substantial gauging scopes.

Time aboard is rarely the constraint in Riga, since loading timber, pellets and grain on the river berths is slow work and many ships lie at the Riga roads anchorage before a berth frees up. In harder winters the Gulf of Riga freezes, ice-class restrictions apply and icebreakers assist traffic, which lengthens stays further. The distinctive inspection issue in Riga is the cargo itself. Wood pellets and wood chips in closed holds produce carbon monoxide and consume oxygen, so the holds, and stairways and spaces next to them, must be ventilated and tested before anyone enters to gauge. Timber deck cargoes load lashing points and deck plating, and grab discharge of bulk cargoes damages hold frames and tank tops. A Riga UTM scope is therefore planned around atmosphere testing and cargo damage as much as corrosion.

facilities.h: Where ships are gauged in Riga
p: Almost all gauging in Riga is done alongside the river terminals or at the anchorage. Because terminals are spread over a long stretch of river on both banks, the team plans each day around one ship rather than moving between berths, and the agent arranges ISPS passes terminal by terminal. Bulk and timber ships are gauged hold by hold as cargo operations allow, starting with the holds that will be loaded last. Container feeders are measured during their scheduled calls, which are shorter, so their scopes are tighter and prepared in advance with the ship's officers.

Ships that will dock elsewhere in the Baltic after leaving Riga benefit from pre-docking gauging here. Measured renewal figures let the owner place the docking with a firm steel list and compare yard offers on the same basis. For ships at the roads anchorage, a launch takes the team out; work there is limited to deck, piping and gas-freed ballast tanks, and depends on weather and, in hard winters, ice. Ultrasonic thickness measurement in Riga is often the first job on a Baltic round.
list: Bulk and timber terminals on the lower Daugava — bulk carriers and general cargo ships; hold frames, hopper plating and tank tops gauged between loading stages
Riga container terminals — feeder ships on Baltic and North Sea loops; deck, hatch-coaming and ballast-tank gauging during their calls
Liquid bulk berths — product tankers; deck plating and cargo and ballast piping gauged under the ship's and terminal's permit systems
Wood pellet and chip berths — bulk carriers loading biomass; hold and adjacent-space gauging only after ventilation and gas testing

context.h: Latvian regulation, ice and trade context for Riga
p: Latvia is a Paris MoU state. Fuel burned in the Gulf of Riga, as everywhere in the Baltic, is capped at 0.10% sulphur under the SECA rules. Bulk carriers and feeders calling at Riga include ships fitted with exhaust gas scrubbers, whose discharge lines, and the shell connection where they leave the ship, need gauging as part of routine maintenance. Since 2024 the EU ETS has counted all emissions on voyages between Riga and other EU ports and half of those on voyages from outside the EU, and FuelEU Maritime has applied since 2025; both raise the stakes when an owner decides whether an older bulk carrier is worth renewing.

Bulk carriers calling at Riga are surveyed under the IACS ESP rules, UR Z10.2 for single-skin and Z10.5 for double-skin ships, with the gauging of cargo holds, double bottoms and the hopper and topside tanks growing at each renewal survey. Ships around their third renewal survey and beyond face the heaviest gauging. Ice is the seasonal factor: the Gulf of Riga does not freeze every winter, but in hard ones the Latvian authorities set ice-class restrictions for the port and icebreakers escort ships into the river. Bulk carrier thickness measurement in Riga is usually timed to the loading programme and, in winter, to the ice.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Riga
jobs.p: Riga work is dominated by dry cargo ships, with gauging fitted into loading programmes on the river. Atmosphere safety comes first wherever biomass is involved, and timber and grab damage shape the scope. A ship inspection in Riga can also serve as the first leg of a wider Baltic round, combining several ships in one mobilisation. Scopes are agreed with the chief officer on arrival so that cargo work is never held up.
list: ESP renewal-survey gauging of a bulk carrier's cargo holds, hopper and topside tanks while she loads grain at a Daugava terminal
Close-up survey support in a timber carrier's holds and on deck, covering lashing pads, deck plating and hatch coamings worn by timber cargo
Pre-purchase gauging of a general cargo ship at the Riga roads anchorage, reporting deck, hold and ballast-tank wastage to the buyer's technical team
Scrubber wash-water piping and overboard discharge line on a container feeder at a Riga container terminal, measured during her scheduled call
Hold and tank gauging on a ship discharging or loading wood pellets, after the holds are ventilated and the atmosphere tested for carbon monoxide and oxygen

logistics: The team lands at Riga International Airport, which lies close to the city and the river terminals. Terminal gate passes under the ISPS Code are requested through the ship's agent, and for ships at the Riga roads the agent also arranges a launch. Latvia is part of the Schengen area, so our technicians from India travel on a Schengen visa and we set the job date once the loading programme or docking slot is firm. Riga is also a convenient start point for jobs further along the coast at Ventspils, Liepāja or Klaipėda.

faqs.q: Is it safe to gauge holds that have carried wood pellets?
faqs.a: Only after the ship has ventilated the holds and tested the atmosphere. Wood pellets give off carbon monoxide and consume oxygen in closed spaces, and the risk extends to stairways and spaces connected to the hold. We work under the ship's enclosed space entry procedure, enter only with valid test results and a permit, and carry personal gas monitors throughout.

faqs.q: Can bulk carrier gauging be done during loading in Riga?
faqs.a: Largely, yes. We gauge holds before loading starts or once they are emptied, starting with the holds that will be loaded last, and measure hopper and topside tanks through their manholes when the crew has certified them safe. Tank tops under cargo cannot be reached, so they are either measured before loading or left for the next discharge or docking.

faqs.q: Does winter ice in the Gulf of Riga affect jobs?
faqs.a: In some winters. When the gulf freezes, ships may wait for icebreaker escort and berthing times move, so we plan with a margin and keep in close contact with the agent. Work inside holds and tanks is unaffected apart from cold-weather couplant. External hull readings from the quay or a launch are limited in ice and are better left for the drydock.

faqs.q: Do you gauge timber deck-cargo fittings?
faqs.a: Yes. On timber carriers we measure deck plating around lashing pads, eyes and stanchion sockets, hatch coamings and the hatch cover edges that take lashing loads. Where welds at lashing points show signs of cracking, magnetic particle testing confirms whether a crack is present and how long it is, so the owner can arrange repairs before the next timber voyage.
